page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-64 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n2d family. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU capabilities. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 86,418.33 and a Passmark CPU score of 62,086.52, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Cached memory bandwidth is highly efficient at 4,066.4 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to average tiers of 132.04 GB/sec and 59.49 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic execution is a notable strength, supported by hardware-level AES and VAES instructions, resulting in a strong Passmark encryption score of 68,639.91.

The primary architectural tradeoff of this instance is its low memory density, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory caching. However, the high compute density makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads. It is well-suited for ray tracing, image processing, multi-threaded decompression, and compute-heavy batch processing.
